column17: Hundreds of people from various Native American tribes gathered at the Nisqually Reservation on Tuesday in observance of Missing and Murdered Indigenous Persons (MMIP) Awareness Day.
column19: Many of them wore red clothing and used red face paint, a powerful symbol of theNative Americans whose voices have been silenced, a defining element of the event.
column21: The demonstration on the Nisqually Reservation dates to 2020, and saw a stronger turnout after 21-year-old Rayandlee Perez was murdered in 2023.
column23: Washington State is believed to have one of the highest numbers of cases, with 134 knownmissing Native Americans as of April 2023, according to the Associated Press.
